title: Conditions this build can code
binding: a questionnaire question's `answer_value_set`, when the answer carries the concept
source: NOT A PRIMARY HEALTH CENTRE DIAGNOSIS LIST, and must not be read as one. These are the clinical findings that appear in the NRCeS India FHIR R4 implementation guide's own OPConsultRecord example, Bundle-OPConsultNote-example-05, read 2026-10-31 through the abdm-docs server's get_fhir_example, which is the only source for a condition code this build could resolve. No authoritative list of the conditions an Indian primary health centre records was reachable, and inventing one is forbidden: a diagnosis list presented as a formulary decides what a clinician can say. So the list is short on purpose and the designed fallback stands, which is that an uncoded diagnosis is narrative text and the note still reaches ABDM. NEEDS SIGN-OFF from a named clinical officer, against a published list, before this is a picker anybody uses.
verified: every concept confirmed to be in http://snomed.info/sct?fhir_vs=isa/404684003, SNOMED CT release http://snomed.info/sct/900000000000207008/version/20250201, through tx.fhir.org
semantic_tags_source: The SNOMED CT semantic tags a candidate for this value set may carry. A codification service returns a concept's semantic tag beside its code, and a candidate whose tag is not in this list is refused before anything else looks at it, so a procedure cannot be offered as a diagnosis and a dose form cannot be offered as a medicine. THIS IS NOT A CLAIM ABOUT EVERY DESCENDANT OF THE BRANCH: it is the set of tags the concepts in this file actually carry, the full specified name of every concept in this file was read from tx.fhir.org on 2026-10-31, SNOMED CT release http://snomed.info/sct/900000000000207008/version/20250201, and the tag in its brackets is recorded below. A legitimate concept under some other tag is therefore refused too, and that is the direction to be wrong in: refusing a real candidate costs a picker, offering a procedure as a diagnosis costs a record.
